articles.title: The OLED Xbox Ally X20 is so good, Asus will sell it solo
articles.summary: Asus’ new Xbox Ally X20 has an OLED screen among other improvements, and the company will now sell it without requiring you to buy a pricey bundle.
articles.body: When I first told you about the “OLED Xbox Ally X of my dreams,” I had to curb my enthusiasm a bit. That’s partly because I hadn’t yet tried the handheld myself, and partly because Asus was only planning to sell it bundled with a pair of expensive AR glasses! I’m happy to say both things are no longer true. Asus will sell a standalone version of the OLED Ally as well, spokesperson Anthony Spence confirms to The Verge. “We are actively discussing the release schedule for a standalone version of the new Ally. Please stay tuned for upcoming announcements.” And after spending two hours with the OLED Ally at the company’s California offices, I think it might even give the new MSI Claw 8 EX AI Plus a run for its money. [Image: [Image: Today, the $1,000 Asus Xbox Ally X is suddenly the best deal in town because of RAMageddon, while the MSI Claw 8 EX offers a generational leap in performance for those who have a staggering $1,800 to spend. But the OLED Ally might offer a third choice for deep-pocketed gamers: the most comfortable and refined handheld yet. A clearer screen I already prefer Asus’ 7.4-inch OLED screen over the 8.8-inch one that Lenovo picked for the Legion Go 2 — yes, the one I previously called “the best handheld screen money can buy.” And I definitely prefer it over the MSI Claw 8 EX’s 8-inch IPS panel. Even though the Ally’s screen is smaller, shorter, and slightly lower resolution — 1080p rather than 1200p — it is so much clearer in person because of its anti-glare cover glass and the brighter panel underneath. [Image: So much more glare on the MSI Claw (top) than the Ally X20 (bottom). Not sure why the Ally has higher-res textures here, though. I brought along a Legion Go 2 and a Claw 8 EX to compare directly to the OLED Xbox Ally X20. With harsh overhead indoor lighting, I had to look through the reflection of my own face on rivals’ glassy screens, but the OLED Ally’s was crystal clear. And while it’s only a little brighter than the Legion Go 2, with 1,400-nit peaks instead of 1,000-nit peaks, it’s much brighter than the Claw EX’s 500-nit screen. I recently took a road trip with the Claw EX and had to squint even at max brightness because of all the glare. A 7.4-inch screen may not sound much bigger than the 7-inch ones on previous Allys, but it makes a difference. Those earlier ones feel a little claustrophobic for me after testing 8-inch handhelds, but I didn’t feel that at all in my couple hours with the Ally X20. Even comfier controls [Image: The translucent frame now has distinct grip components. Last year’s Xbox Ally X showed me that handhelds are better with prongs, and I have to hand it to the MSI Claw EX for adding manta ray fins for an even beefier grip. But Asus now has cushy rubberized grips, too, rather than simply a textured plastic shell, for even more comfort. [Image: The MSI Claw 8 EX with stippled hard plastic grip (left) versus the Ally X20 with rubberized grip (right). The new ABXY face buttons are the most satisfying ones I’ve felt on a handheld yet, quieter, and flush with the handheld’s shell when you press them down. The bumpers feel slightly better, and the screen doesn’t get quite as hot in use due to the reworked fans and airflow. I’m not sure about the triggers yet; I don’t like the squeak my Xbox Ally X review unit’s triggers developed, and these ones feel pretty similar. [Image: The face buttons are notably improved. But I’m so happy to say my old nemesis, the Xbox Ally X “Library” button, is well and truly dead. When I accidentally pressed the new “Action” button that replaces it (it’s the upper-right gold button with a picture of a single horizontal bar), it simply took a screenshot instead of yanking me out of my game. I still think the Start button should be the top button, though. The trick D-pad really works A transforming D-pad that spins to go from eight-way to four-way by lowering four of its corners? I was ready to write it off as a gimmick — until I fired up Hollow Knight: Silksong. It was instantly the difference between nailing every single one of Hornet’s diagonal attacks, letting her float and sting again and again, or me sometimes missing the diagonal input and watching my warrior fall to the ground. [Image: [Image: Sliding image comparison: Drag the handle left and right to see how the D-pad changes. You transform it by pulling up on the D-pad’s horizontal edge with your fingernails and rotating it a quarter-turn. Hopefully it doesn’t become an extra point of mechanical failure; it felt tight and premium to me. The clicky dome switches underneath won’t satisfy those who prefer membrane D-pads, but I like it. How about performance? Asus wasn’t ready to let me run true benchmarks, but I did fire up two games on the Xbox Ally X20 and the MSI Claw 8 EX for direct comparisons, setting both processors to 25 watts and loading the same exact save. In Cyberpunk 2077, the Claw EX offered 61 frames per second in the same location that the Ally X20 offered 44fps. In Returnal, the Claw EX offered 62fps where the Ally X20 offered 41. Both handhelds drained their battery at roughly the same rate of 36 watts, meaning their 80-watt-hour batteries should last about two hours on a charge. [Image: Returnal on the MSI Claw EX (top) and the Ally X20 (bottom). That means the Claw may have 40 or 50 percent more performance with no battery penalty — but it’s not the whole story. First, the OLED Ally has a 30–120Hz variable refresh rate (VRR) screen, meaning it should look smoother at even lower frame rates than the 48–120Hz panels in the Claw EX and the original Ally. It definitely seemed smooth in my brief demo. Second, as I’ll eventually discuss in my full Claw EX review, that Intel chip is having some growing pains with drivers. You may even be able to see it in my Returnal comparison photo in this story: There’s less volumetric fog and less ground cover than you see with the AMD chip in the Ally. I’m also experiencing stutter or uneven frame pacing in some games with the Intel Claw, like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, where I’ll get more than 50fps but they still don’t always feel smooth, and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle keeps freezing on me entirely. Intel tells me it’s working on issues like these, though, and its latest drivers have already fixed most of the Expedition 33 graphical glitches we saw on Intel. Third, the Ally’s fans were notably quieter than the Claw’s during these two tests. [Image: The Ally X20 is a tad heavier than the Xbox Ally X, but still fits the same Mechanism third-party mounting grips and stands. Because of RAMageddon, every gaming handheld is too expensive today, and the OLED Ally will surely be the same. It’s almost certain to cost more than today’s $1,000 Xbox Ally X, so I wouldn’t wait for this new one if that’s as much as you’re willing to spend. But if you’re looking for the best handheld at any price, the OLED Ally might be worth waiting for. Photography by Sean Hollister / The Verge

articles.title: The 'Father of PlayStation' Says Killing Discs Backlash Is a 'Mentality Issue'
articles.summary: Ken Kutaragi, known as "The Father of PlayStation," has backed Sony's controversial decision to scrap discs on PS5. Kutaragi, who ran Sony's gaming business through its first three console generations, told VGC that while he understands the backlash, it isn't “economically reasonable.”
articles.body:
Ken Kutaragi, known as "The Father of PlayStation," has backed Sony's controversial decision to scrap discs on PS5. Kutaragi, who ran Sony's gaming business through its first three console generations, told VGC that while he understands the backlash, it isn't “economically reasonable.”

“Although we had network capability back in the PS2 and PS3 days, it was not that common [as it is today]. Now, many, many people are connected,” he said.

“I understand that physical discs have become a metaphor for ‘owning’ games. I really understand that mentality… But nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content. So it’s a mentality.

“I really understand [why some people are upset], but I don’t think it’s economically reasonable. Maybe it’s a mentality issue.”

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

While Kutaragi noted that Sony's decision had caused friction for players, he pointed at the makeup of Sony Interactive Entertainment, which employs people from streaming services such as Gaikai. Kutaragi noted that Sony might have ambitions wider than just gaming with its all-digital plans.

He went on to suggest consoles could eventually be phased out, with platform holders utilizing streaming solutions to combat the rising price of components (thanks, AI). “We won’t need any console,” he said, before he clarified: “This isn’t an official comment from Sony Computer Entertainment!”

Under Sony’s current plans, physical discs on PlayStation consoles will be phased out entirely by 2028 . Sony reportedly knew killing PS5 discs would be a huge PR problem , but it is pressing ahead. Sony’s rationale for ditching discs is that it’s simply following consumer trends. “In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only,” Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog .

“As consumer preferences and the broader entertainment industry continue to shift away from physical discs to digital, physical game disc production for all new games releasing on PlayStation consoles will be discontinued starting January 2028. Following this date, new games will be available on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. This transition has no impact on games that already released, or will be releasing, prior to January 2028 in disc format.

“This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs. This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today."

Players have been using any platform they can, including PlayStation surveys , to let their preservation concerns be heard.

Photo by Stephen Shugerman/Getty Images.

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Street Fighter’s 4K Steelbook Is Up for Preorder, and Comes in Champion or Villain Variants
articles.summary: Street Fighter’s 4K Steelbook Edition asks fans to choose between a special edition champion or villain variant cover, with preorders now live at Amazon.
articles.body:
Street Fighter officially hits movie theaters today, but some retailers are wasting no time in getting its physical version up for preorder.

Standard 4Ks are now available to buy from a couple of different retailers, but the film is also getting a very fun Amazon-exclusive 4K steelbook that comes in two different variants for you to choose from: Champion or Villain .

Preorder Street Fighter Amazon Exclusive 4K Steelbook

Of course, a release date is not yet available for these since the movie only just released in theaters. Same goes for any information on bonus features.

However, once they've been revealed, we'll be sure to update this. For now, take a look at these awesome 4Ks and be quick to grab your favorites.

The steelbooks, in particular, could very well sell out, so don't wait too long to put in a preorder.

Depending on which steelbook you buy, you'll have a different collection of characters gracing the cover.

As you'd expect, these are either champions or villains, which is a fun way to split up a steelbook release like this. In general, it's quite a vibrant cover as well, so it's sure to be a standout in your movie library.

These are listed for $47.99, but prices may come down between now and release, which you're guaranteed to get with Amazon. Plus, as a reminder, Amazon won't charge you for this preorder until the item ships either.

Preorder Street Fighter – Standard Edition

If you're not interested in the steelbook and just looking for a regular ol' 4K to buy, Amazon and Walmart both have copies up right now to preorder for $38.99.

This cover is a lot less crowded than the steelbook above, but still features the vibrant red background with 'Street Fighter' in bright yellow across the top.

While its physical release is likely still a long ways away, this is the perfect time to catch the movie in theaters.

If that's part of your weekend plan and you're curious what to expect, IGN's Tom Jorgensen said in his review that it's "dumber than a box of rocks, but have you ever thrown rocks at things? It can be pretty fun with the right combination of enthusiastic friends and anarchic spirit."

And if you're looking to buy some more 4Ks and Blu-rays, check out our rundown of what's releasing soon to stock up.

articles.title: I Bought a Steam Machine – Here’s Why (and How It’s Going)
articles.summary: I bought a Steam Machine, despite the high price. Here's why I have no regrets.
articles.body:
To buy a Steam Machine, you first must join a waitlist.

I signed up on a lark. I wasn't actually going to buy one. I had already resigned myself to playing PC games on my TV via my docked Steam Deck . That is, when I wasn’t playing my PS5, Xbox Series X, or Switch 2. The last thing I needed was another gaming device attached, through a tangle of cables, to the back of my TV.

Despite all this, I joined the Steam Machine waitlist (for the 512GB model with a Steam Controller) – and then quickly forgot all about it.

So I was surprised when my purchase email arrived roughly 10 weeks later. Once your email arrives, you have three days to place your order, or you lose your chance to buy.

Upon reading the email, I was sure I wasn’t going to buy it. Between the Steam Machine’s high price and my ability to play nearly any game I want on my other consoles, it would be a pricy and unnecessary addition to my gaming life.

Even though I wasn’t going to buy a Steam Machine, I kept thinking about it over my three-day purchase window. I watched and read reviews , mentally noting the pros and cons, trying to determine if, actually, maybe I should buy one?

Ever since I bought Valve's handheld Steam Deck in 2022, it's been my platform of choice. I’ve managed to accrue a large library of Steam games over the years, and it annoyed me that more power-hungry games don't run well or look good when played on a TV via the docked Steam Deck.

But I loved the PC platform, which offers endless backward compatibility and the ease of emulating older consoles. SteamOS is a marvelous thing that combines the convenience of a console with the versatility of a PC.

Meanwhile, Sony and Microsoft haven’t exactly been endearing themselves to gamers of this generation. Killer first-party games have been few and far between. Both companies have been laying off employees and closing or offloading studios. Both still charge a monthly fee for online play. And Sony’s decision to cease production of discs in January 2028 has riled fans against the company in a way I can’t remember ever seeing before.

None of this makes me eager to hop onboard with whatever these companies are cooking up for next-gen. Valve, on the other hand – while not perfect – has been much more consumer-friendly.

In the end, just a few hours before my purchase window lapsed, I ordered a Steam Machine. And I love the thing.

While I had some initial problems trying to play older games that don’t support Steam cloud saves (and thus couldn’t pick up the progress I’d made on Steam Deck), I downloaded a handful of newer games (The Witcher 3 Remastered, The Order of the Sinking Star, ARC Raiders) and have been playing happily across devices.

It's no more powerful than my other consoles, but it has my main library of games on it, and it runs them beautifully on my 4K TV. The Steam Controller immediately became my favorite game controller, supplanting the Xbox controller I had always preferred before.

As it stands now, hardware-wise, I might be done with Sony and Microsoft going forward. I'll play the majority of games on my Steam Machine/Deck combo. I'll play Nintendo's first-party gems on my Switch 2. And when the PS6 arrives, whenever that may be and however much it may cost, it almost certainly won't be a day-one purchase for me.

Is the Steam Machine is pricy for what it offers? Yes. Is it right for everyone? Absolutely not. But it's right for IGN's tech editor Jackie Thomas . And as someone who’s been buying 99% of my games on PC and Switch over the past few years, it's right for me.

articles.title: Ghost of Yotei Sales Lag Behind Tsushima but Are Still Strong on PS5, Analyst Estimates Show
articles.summary: Ghost of Yōtei sales appear to be trailing behind Ghost of Tsushima, but that doesn't mean it's not still pulling big numbers on PlayStation 5.
articles.body:
Ghost of Yōtei sales appear to be trailing behind Ghost of Tsushima , but that doesn't mean it's not still pulling big numbers on PlayStation 5.

That's according to Alinea Analytics head of marketing analysis Rhys Elliott, who shared data related to Sucker Punch Productions' 2025 sequel on X/Twitter . Although this is sales information that has yet to be confirmed by Sony, it may still give us a peek behind the curtain at how Ghost of Yōtei has fared on PS5.

The result: Sucker Punch's action follow-up has done well in its first year, even if it hasn't quite managed to pass up its predecessor. Alinea's analysis puts Ghost of Yōtei sales at about 5.4 million units, generating $407 million in revenue so far. Highlights from that update put the physical slice at a notable 36.8%, while PlayStation Store discounts remain largely few and far between.

Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Screenshots

Around 500,000 copies were sold in Q3 2026 alone. Alinea also reported that 50,000 players have picked up the digital Complete Edition – which comes with new content, including the recently released Echoes of Sekigahara expansion – in the two weeks since PlayStation launched it as a replacement for the digital base game. With the analysis estimating that around 6% of its existing base returned to play the new content, it seems Ghost of Yōtei is going strong – but there is more to the story.

Ghost of Tsushima, which launched in a market still coming to grips with pandemic lockdowns in July 2020, had generated about $418 million by the same point in its lifespan, Elliott added in a follow-up post. Factoring in Yōtei's base price of $70 vs Tsushima's base price of $60, as well as any discounts that followed, the latter is estimated to have sold almost 7 million copies by this point.

That puts Tsushima moving at a much faster pace in terms of raw units sold, but there is more at play here, especially considering revenue is almost neck and neck.

How do Ghost of Yotei’s revenues compare to Tsushima’s? Our estimates (@alineaanalytics) show that Yotei has generated revenue of $407M. At this point, launch-aligned, Ghost of Tsushima had made $418M, so about 3% more. As Yotei costs $70, and has had just two discounts, and Tsushima was $60 at launch (and was already discounted to $45 less than three months post-launch), Tsushima had sold more copies at this point. Nearly 7M versus Yotei’s 5.4M. This is about 26% more revenue per buyer, which is consistent with PlayStation’s goal of extracting more revenue per player. While that’s quite the gap in terms of copies, it’s worth noting that by this point in Tsushima’s lifecycle, there were about 117M PS4s and 10M PS5s in the wild, versus the nearly 100M PS5s currently out there right now (Yotei’s only platform). That said, Yotei’s revenue is beginning to flatten more than Tsushima’s did, but perhaps the GTA-driven influx of new PS5s will soften that. Yotei has proven to be an evergreen seller in a crowded market, shifting 1.8M copies this year ($121M in revenue) despite having just two small discounts and competing with what is one of the busiest and highest-quality release calendars … ever. So yeah, anyone who says that Ghost of Yotei is a flop is flat-out wrong. (Note: the Y-axis starts at $392M. Otherwise, the chart wouldn’t be readable, as the numbers are so close) — Rhys Elliott (@superhys) October 16, 2026

How do Ghost of Yotei’s revenues compare to Tsushima’s? Our estimates (@alineaanalytics) show that Yotei has generated revenue of $407M. At this point, launch-aligned, Ghost of Tsushima had made $418M, so about 3% more. As Yotei costs $70, and has had just two discounts, and Tsushima was $60 at launch (and was already discounted to $45 less than three months post-launch), Tsushima had sold more copies at this point. Nearly 7M versus Yotei’s 5.4M. This is about 26% more revenue per buyer, which is consistent with PlayStation’s goal of extracting more revenue per player. While that’s quite the gap in terms of copies, it’s worth noting that by this point in Tsushima’s lifecycle, there were about 117M PS4s and 10M PS5s in the wild, versus the nearly 100M PS5s currently out there right now (Yotei’s only platform). That said, Yotei’s revenue is beginning to flatten more than Tsushima’s did, but perhaps the GTA-driven influx of new PS5s will soften that. Yotei has proven to be an evergreen seller in a crowded market, shifting 1.8M copies this year ($121M in revenue) despite having just two small discounts and competing with what is one of the busiest and highest-quality release calendars … ever. So yeah, anyone who says that Ghost of Yotei is a flop is flat-out wrong. (Note: the Y-axis starts at $392M. Otherwise, the chart wouldn’t be readable, as the numbers are so close)

"While that’s quite the gap in terms of copies, it’s worth noting that by this point in Tsushima’s lifecycle, there were about 117M PS4s and 10M PS5s in the wild, versus the nearly 100M PS5s currently out there right now (Yōtei's only platform)," Elliott explained. "That said, Yōtei's revenue is beginning to flatten more than Tsushima’s did, but perhaps the GTA-driven influx of new PS5s will soften that."

In other words, although Ghost of Tsushima had managed to move more copies by this point after its launch, Ghost of Yōtei is holding its own. Early estimates after the sequel's launch also had it falling in line with the original game , with Sony going on to confirm in February of this year that the follow-up "exceeded" Tsushima's sales and "significantly contributed" to its financial results for that quarter. As Elliott clarified today, "anyone who says that Ghost of Yōtei is a flop is flat-out wrong."

Ghost of Yōtei launched in October 2025 and is exclusive to PS5. IGN gave it an 8/10 review , saying, "A predictable but well-executed story takes you through Ghost of Yotei's gorgeous landscapes and satisfying, fluid action – it may not be revolutionizing open world games, but it's a great distillation of the samurai fantasy." articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 – Captain Price's Fate Explained
articles.summary: Who is alive and who is dead at the end of Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4's campaign? Infinity Ward explains Captain Price's fate.
articles.body:
Is Captain Price dead? It’s a reasonable question to have at the end of Modern Warfare 4’s campaign, considering how often characters we thought were gone have come back over the course of the four-game story — I’ve lost track of the number of times Graves has returned now. We spoke to developer Infinity Ward to get an answer, and we got one. Well, kind of.

In a mid-credits scene, Mads Mikkelsen’s The Archer can be seen taking a captive Captain Price away on a truck. An ambush allows Price to break free, though, as the vehicle crashes, leaving The Archer to scuttle away into the snow as our hero wrestles with a metal pipe sticking out of his stomach. After stumbling after the villain, Price turns the tables on him and uses said pipe to puncture his throat, leaving the rogue Russian minister of defense very much dead in the middle of a frozen-over lake. Ghost then arrives on the scene to share his former squadmate's final breaths with him as Price lies still, presumably dead, next to his victim. But is he?

I asked Jeff Negus, narrative director at Infinity Ward, if that’s the case. “I'll say this. We went out of our way in this game to pace character deaths, both in where they happen and in the expression of the moment happening,” explains Negus. “And I would say that scene is consistent with others.”

So, not a yes or a no, is it? Multiple characters established in earlier series entries meet their makers across Modern Warfare 4’s 16 missions, including Makarov, Gabriela, Graves, and Gaz, to name but a few. While we don’t see any of them put in the ground never to rise again, some of them meet pretty conclusive ends, with the Gs — Gaz, Graves, and Gabriela — all receiving bullets to the head. Makarov's head is now pulp on a snowy New York street, but he looked pretty lifeless the last time we saw him, and seeing as he’s dispatched so early in the story, surely he would’ve come back by now. Archer needs a reason to go after Price and avenge his son, after all.

If Price does indeed meet an end “consistent with others,” then surely this means he is dead. It would seem like a fitting place for the Modern Warfare reboot saga to end, and feel like an actual definite conclusion. But we know things are never that simple when it comes to Call of Duty, and I can see why the door may be left slightly ajar for him to come back if needed. If MW4 is well-received critically and proves a commercial success, Activision would want to keep things rolling.

For my money, I’d say he’s dead. He’s achieved what he set out to do at the start of Modern Warfare 4’s story, and has even learned a lesson or two about selflessness along the way. It’s the basics of any hero’s journey, and it ended in glorious sacrifice, taking down a threat to the Western world in the form of The Archer’s diabolical plan. What do you think? Has Captain Price died? Let us know in the comments.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: PlayStation 6 Will Likely Have Sony's Own Take on Frame Generation, According to Latest Patent
articles.summary: Frame generation is established tech in games at this point, and we already knew that Sony was looking at the tecnology for the PlayStation 6, but the company has filed a new patent that gives a better idea of how it'll work.
articles.body:
Frame generation is established tech in games at this point. We already knew that Sony was looking at the tecnology for the PlayStation 6 , but the company has filed a new patent that gives a better idea of how it'll work.

The patent, titled "Generation Super Sampling," (US-20260320740-A1 ), describes a mostly standard form of frame generation, where the model takes information from a traditionally rendered frame and then uses that information to generate an interpolated frame. The major difference is in how the model will be predicting how the frames will change.

DLSS frame generation works by taking rendered frames and then pulling motion vector information from the game engine. The suggested PlayStation model will also take input data from your controller to more accurately predict how you're going to be moving from frame to frame. The hope, according to the patent notes, is to limit the amount of latency or 'hitching' from frame to frame.

Sony PlayStation Frame Generation Patent

The patent also leaves the door open for multi-frame generation, which was introduced on PC with the RTX 5090 back in 2025. According to the patent notes, "In some embodiments, the predictions are not limited to an immediate next image in the image stream. The decoder system may be trained to predict any number of images before or after the input image."

It's hard to imagine why a console that'd presumably be attached to a TV needs to generate multiple frames, though. With PC gaming, multi-frame generation is only really useful when you're playing on a super-high refresh rate gaming monitor at 144Hz or higher. Even the TVs that do support high refresh rates are limited to 120Hz, which really limits the need for multi-frame generation. Still, having the option wouldn't be terrible.

My only concern with bringing frame generation to consoles is whether or not users will be able to turn it on or off at will. The nightmare scenario in my head is developers using it as a crutch, forcing it on to hit 30 or 60 fps in a game that'd otherwise be getting 15–20 fps. That kind of solution would introduce a ton of latency and visual artifacts, but then again, it's possible that taking user inputs into the frame gen pipeline could alleviate that issue.

Sony has been on a tear lately with its patents, and it really does seem like the company is building up to its next generation of consoles. Last month, it filed a patent that described an AI agent keeping an eye on your system and deploying fixes before you even notice a problem. Then, there was a patent that would implement an NFC reader into your PlayStation controller and would enable tap-to-pay. Because these are all only patents, there is a chance that none of these technologies see the light of day, but either way, the PlayStation 6 is turning out to be quite the interesting console to say the least.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Dragon Ball’s Goku Voice Actor 'Furious' Over AI Videos Using Her Voice Without Permission
articles.summary: Masako Nozawa, best known for voicing Goku in the Dragon Ball anime series, is slamming AI users for stealing her voice to create projects using the rapidly-advancing technology, calling it outright “theft.”
articles.body:
Masako Nozawa, best known for voicing Goku in the Dragon Ball anime series, is slamming AI users for stealing her voice to create projects using the rapidly advancing technology, calling it outright “theft.”

If you’re an anime fan, you’ve likely seen a few fan-made videos that use AI to copy characters’ voices, making them say some absolutely outrageous stuff. This trend isn't limited to English-speaking fanbases; it's also happening quite frequently in Japan, to the point where voice actors have gathered together to create the country’s first-ever guidelines regarding the use of AI voices.

Perhaps the most prominent of these actors is 89-year-old Nozawa. She’s a prolific voice actor who has been working in the space for decades and is best known as the voice of Goku (as well as Son Gohan and oodles of Goku variants) in Dragon Ball .

In an October 15 interview with Japanese outlet NHK , Nozawa was shown an AI video that used her voice — and her response to it was nothing short of scathing.

"That's not my voice,” she told the outlet. “I can't forgive them for using it without permission; it's like theft, and it makes me furious. I believe my voice and my acting are my own. If they're going to use even a little bit of it, they should get my permission.

"The AI-generated voice may resemble me. It may even be identical. But it lacks heart, doesn't it? Without heart, it's no good, no matter what the role. Even if it's just a crying voice, I believe it's different if you cry with emotion."

On September 30, the Tokyo District Court ruled that the unauthorized use of someone’s voice infringes upon their right to publicity in a landmark decision for both the voice acting industry and AI regulations as a whole. It’s one of Japan’s first major protections against AI, and it follows a lawsuit from famous voice actor Kenjiro Tsuda against TikTok over a video that used AI to imitate his voice.

"Rules are now being established, so I hope everyone will follow them. It's all based on the premise that everyone will truly follow the rules,” Nozawa said of this ruling.

Rather than relying on AI, Nozawa encourages fans to work hard to become voice actors themselves. "I want you to work hard so that you become someone people will definitely remember as a voice actor,” she said. “If you don't put your heart into it, you'll just be reading the lines, so make them come alive."

Nozawa is vice-chairperson for the Japan Actors Union, which held a press conference on October 15 to discuss its new guidelines regarding AI voices. "The progress of AI is amazing, isn't it?” Nozawa said in a statement. “It feels like the things I dreamed of as a child are becoming reality one after another, and it excites me. But it's disillusioning when it's being used without permission. I hope that everyone will follow the rules and we can create a future where both humans and AI can have fun together."

She isn’t the only prominent voice actor with something to say about AI; Toshi Shimada, best known for his role as Tomozo in the anime Chibi Maruko-chan, said that he “simply cannot accept the idea of ​​creating words I never said and songs I never sang, and then trying to monetize them. What I fear most is that the voice acting industry will collapse if unauthorized AI voices continue to be uploaded."

Michihiro Ikemizu, another prominent voice actor and Vice Chairman of the Union, explained that the “biggest problem is that people will lose their jobs. We want to build a track record with these guidelines and eventually aim for legislation."

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus SUPER GEKITOU Trailer - Screenshots

This is the latest big news to come from AI voice acting after Amazon Prime Video caused a kerfuffle for introducing an AI-generated English dub of the anime Banana Fish back in 2025. The decision caused so much backlash that the streamer eventually removed it , but many fans felt that the fact it was included at all didn't bode well for the future of the dubbing industry.

articles.title: Pokémon Reveals New 'Holiday Helper’ Plush Collection With a Christmas Tree Pikachu and Clodsire Sled
articles.body:
Pokémon has revealed a new collection of “Holiday Helper” plushies.

Pokémon shared an image of the new collection across the company's social accounts earlier today. The image shows five festive Pikachu plushies in varying sizes, including a Pikachu with a Clodsire sled.

A blog post on the official Japanese Pokémon website offers a closer look at the new plushies while confirming that the collection will be released in local Pokémon Center locations on October 24. North American Pokémon accounts only confirmed that the new plushies are “coming soon” to the U.S. via the Pokémon Center, which dropped the first wave of its 2026 holiday collection earlier this week.

Pokémon Reveals 'Holiday Helpers' Plush Collection Coming Soon to U.S.

The biggest plush in the image is a chunky Pikachu dressed in a full Christmas tree outfit, complete with a little star on his head.

The smaller Pikachu plushies, which additional images reveal are actually keychains, have the Electric type making various expressions in a Santa hat. A sleepy Pikachu holds a small cookie, a cutesy Pikachu is covered in snow, and a particularly mischievous Pikachu is riding a Porygon.

At a glance, it looks like Santa Clodsire is his own plush, but the Japanese Pokemon site shows the amphibious Pokémon connected to a small Pikachu riding a sled.

The announcement doesn’t include any information about sizing or pricing, but most plush keychains available on the Pokémon Center are between 4 to 8 inches tall The smaller guys look like they’ll be on the shorter end of that spectrum, which the Pokemon Center generally prices under $20.

The largest plushie's rounded shape is giving Squishmallow, and the Pokémon Center is generally home to the 12-inch Squish models . However, given how large he looks in the reveal image, the Christmas tree Pika could be up to 16 or even 20 inches tall.

The Pokémon Center prices Squishmallows at $29.99, though its self-developed larger plushies can reach up to $79.99. (Without getting into the multi-hundred-dollar life-size collections .)

It remains to be seen whether these Pikachus (and Clodsire) are the full collection of Holiday Helpers, or whether additional Pokémon will get the festive plushie treatment. The announcement also doesn't clarify whether the additional collection items shown in the Japan announcement , like Tangrowth holiday sweaters, will be exclusive to Japan.

The Pokémon Center is home to a ridiculous amount of Pokémon merch, including ongoing collections like the Holiday Village figure series and, of course, some of the best Pokémon plushies money can buy. Fans can look forward to new releases in these collections each holiday season, in addition to more general merch drops throughout the year.

articles.title: What Happened to Modern Technology in Avatar: Seven Havens?
articles.body:
Note : This article contains spoilers for all six episodes of Avatar: Seven Havens.

We're now six episodes into Avatar: Seven Havens and many big questions still remain a mystery. What actually caused the cataclysm? Who are the Faceless? Why are there twin Avatars?

This latest batch of episodes did, however, finally give some hints about what could have happened to modern technology. As you may remember from The Legend of Korra , Republic City was at the heart of an industrial revolution that produced cars, mechs, and even broadcast radio. So what exactly happened in the 225 years since Korra's time to destroy all that?

Before we get into theories about what could have happened, let's dig into what technology we've actually seen in the show so far.

The first few episodes of Seven Havens are completely devoid of any sort of technology, but we get our first glimpse of something in Episode 5 when Pavi and Nisha are digging through relics in Karthik's office. They discover an old radio that appears to still be working and receiving a transmission, presumably from members of the Order of the White Lotus in other Havens. When Chancellor Kayoko finds the radio and accuses Kathik of contacting the other havens, he writes it off as a "broken relic from the old world."

Then later at the end of Episode 6, we get a look at Chancellor Kayoko calling on the other Havens for help via a much more elaborate radio setup. While Karthik is using what appears to be a relic to covertly communicate, it's clear that the Havens have still retained basic broadcast systems to stay in touch. This very much fits the whole "apocalypse" vibe as radio signals rely on lower frequencies and minimal power to send messages across longer distances. The fact that her radio station is hidden in a concealed tower room only helps confirm that this technology is meant to be used sparingly.

The other big clue about technology also comes from Episode 6, where the benders, who appear to be afflicted by the weird red energy, run into what seems to be a generator room. On the way there, they pass a series of flickering lights that show the base is actually being powered by something, rather than relying purely on fire light. It's here that we see the mysterious red energy (which may or may not be Vaatu!) interacting with this power grid.

The generator room appears to be pretty low tech, being reminiscent of the more advanced airships we saw during Avatar Aang's time. This shows that although some form of technology is being used to power Ellora, it's not nearly as advanced as what you'd expect from a society that should be far more industrialized.

Now that we've gotten an idea of what kinds of technology humans are still operating with, we can start making some decent guesses about what actually happened. The most likely reason for the technological collapse goes all the way back to what happened after Korra left the spirit portals open. Giant spirit vines found their way into the world and humans, of course, started using them as a power source. This resulted in a combination of technology and spirit energy that nobody was really prepared for.

We saw the devastating power of this combination in The Legend of Korra when Kuvira harnesses tree roots to power a nuclear-level energy cannon she mounts to a giant mech suit. The only reason that cannon didn't cause the mass destruction it was capable of was because Korra was able to redirect the massive blast with some good old Spiritbending.

So why does all of this matter for Seven Havens? Well, at the end of The Legend of Korra, spirit vine energy is still very much a contentious topic. Korra makes it clear she opposes any further research into the field, and she's backed by the president of Republic City. But it certainly seems like that wasn't the end of all that. Although Seven Havens hasn't yet revealed what actually happened, it seems likely that spirit vine technology was at the heart of it.

The other obvious clue we have to make the case for this is the weird lamp Pavi finds in Karthik's office, among the other relics. It looks like some sort of modern use of spirit vines, suggesting the technology likely became more intertwined with the physcial world.

At the center of every Avatar conflict, there's an issue of balance. For Aang, it was stopping the Fire Nation and bringing balance back to a world at war with itself. For Korra, it was all about bringing back balance between the spirit world and the physical world. Neither Avatar fully succeeded, but Korra's story was left pretty unfinished due to all of the uncertainties after opening up the spiritual floodgates on the world.

The prevailing theory about what caused the cataclysm in Seven Havens, and the one I believe to be most likely, is that the use of spirit vine energy got out of hand. Like any natural resource, abusing it is going to cause some problems and destabilize the balance between the spirit world and the physical world. The cataclysm, in this case, could very likely be the spirit world forcibly trying to rebalance things by destroying humanity and the technology it built.

This theory would explain why the only gadgets we're seeing in Seven Havens appear to be pretty low tech and the Chancellor is pretty careful about using the radio. It would also explain why the mysterious red energy would be some sort of electricity/spirit energy hybrid that only the Avatars can deal with.

While this theory does seem to explain why technology is noticeably absent from the series, it's still only a theory. It's unlikely we'll uncover all of the mysteries in Season 1 , especially now that it’s been renewed through a fourth season . In the meantime, it's certainly enjoyable to dig into what actually happened to the world Korra left behind.

articles.title: True Detective Season 5 Confirms Antonio Banderas and Nicolas Cage as Its Leads
articles.summary: True Detective Season 5 will officially star Antonio Banderas and Nicolas Cage as its two leads.
articles.body:
True Detective Season 5 will officially star Antonio Banderas and Nicolas Cage as its two leads.

The next season of the HBO crime series confirmed the duo today with a video post on social media . Production is expected to begin in 2027, with a more specific release date for the follow-up episodes unclear for now.

True Detective Season 4: Night Country showrunner Issa López is back to serve as showrunner on Season 5. While most plot details remain under wraps this early in development, the next batch of episodes are expected to take place in Jamaica Bay, New York, with Banderas tapped as Rai García and Cage set as Henry Logan, as told by The Hollywood Reporter .

Banderas and Cage are two names that have circulated in the TV rumor mill for some time. Word of Cage's potential involvement surfaced all the way back in August of last year, but updates on that front then went quiet for months. It wasn't until this past weekend that the actor took the stage at New York Comic Con to tease that he was still in the mix.

"So, I think I’m probably going to do another season of television," he told the crowd (via THR). "I think I might do a season of True Detective. That’s OK that I’m the first to announce that, right?"

It wasn't too much of a surprise to hear Cage testing the waters, but confirmation of Banderas' involvement was mostly limited to the odd rumor and never felt quite as certain. Now, both are officially on board.

Cage. Banderas. Season 5 of #TrueDetective starts production in 2027. — True Detective (@TrueDetective) October 16, 2026

Cage. Banderas. Season 5 of #TrueDetective starts production in 2027.

Cage made a name for himself with roles in movies like Raising Arizona, Face/Off, and National Treasure, but most recently appeared in projects like Spider-Noir, Longlegs, and Pig. Banderas' acting career has seen him star in things like The Mask of Zorro and Shrek, with his most recent roles including parts in Tony and Puss in Boots: The Last Wish. With previous seasons of True Detective led by unforgettable duos like Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson (Season 1), and Jodie Foster and Kali Reis (Season 4), HBO is already off to a solid start.

articles.title: ‘There Should be a Game Award for Hot Dads’ — Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Devs Are Fully Aware and Loving the ‘Horny’ Fanart for Their Game
articles.summary: The developers behind Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse are enthusiastic about the “horny” fanart they’ve seen of the game’s characters, saying they specifically made them "hot" to appeal to fans.
articles.body:
The developers behind Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse are enthusiastic about all the “horny” fanart they’ve seen of the game’s characters, saying they specifically made them "hot" to appeal to fans.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse released on October 15, and you’ve no doubt already seen the wealth of wild reactions to the title from players online — particularly in regards to its character designs.

Yes, it’s true; players are thirsty for Trevor Belmont and the various monsters they must fight as they navigate the chaotic streets of Paris, but they shouldn’t feel embarrassed about it. In fact, the devs were counting on this to happen.

Speaking with Fall Damage , marketing director and lead designer Bérenger Dupré and Sandro Bordier revealed that they are absolutely loving the thirsty reactions to the game’s characters — and that includes the “horny” fanart that they’ve seen on social media.

“Oh, it has started already. Like, man, have we seen some things,” Bordier joked.

“Trevor, especially,” Dupré added. “Didn’t realize that he would be so well-received.”

“Do you think we could add a ‘Hot Dads Edition?’” Bourdier asked, prompting Dupré to say that there “should be a Game Award for hot dads.”

“It’s always fun to see the fanart, because we know how important and dear these characters are to the fans. We are trying to make some new, fresh stories with them, so it’s always quite stressful. And for now, the reception is very, very emotional,” Dupré continued.

The duo went on to admit that they went out of their way to make these characters attractive, with Boudier saying, “Yes, like we know some characters are hot. It’s a choice, actually. Like it’s a vibe. We’re pretty proud of it.”

“Honestly, we were super happy with all the fan reactions regarding the characters that were revealed,” he added. “We really put a lot of love from the team to design them in a way that would please fans. We were super happy to see how they reacted to the designs and the voice actor reveals, of course.”

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse released to solid reviews, with IGN’s Scott White scoring the game an eight out of ten , praising it for “bringing Konami’s beloved series into the modern era with a fast-paced focus on action first.”

It’s clear that a lot of love went into this title; among the various Easter Eggs and secret codes found within, the devs also paid homage to classic fighting game characters , which can be seen if players nab a hidden weapon in one of the game’s first areas.

articles.title: Street Fighter: How Can There Be an Ending Explained When There Is No Ending?
articles.summary: Street Fighter is in theaters now, so this is our ending explained... or rather, non-ending explained. Plus, are there any post-credits scenes in the new movie?
articles.body:
Let's make this simple: You want to know if there are any mid- or post-credits scenes in Street Fighter . The answer is yes, as the film features an animated mid-credit scene.

Street Fighter is back on the big screen this week, with the third live-action incarnation of the popular video game franchise after attempts in 1994 and 2009 . Was the third time the charm? Well, as Tom Jorgensen’s Street Fighter review for IGN notes, not exactly, though it’s certainly superior to The Legend of Chun-Li.

So how did things play out in this go-around? The story this time centers on old friends Ken (Noah Centineo) and Ryu (Andrew Koji), who are reunited after a years-long rift when they are both recruited by Chun-Li (Callina Liang) for the second-ever World Warrior tournament, which is being presented by Shadaloo dictator M. Bison (David Dastmalchian).

Soon, the best fighters in the world are gathering in Shadaloo, even as Bison has ulterior motives for holding the tournament at all, as his main goal is to get ahold of Ryu – the winner of the one previous World Warrior – in order to drain his “Hado Power” (which gives Ryu the rare ability to create a Hadouken) for himself.

So how did the tournament play out? And who had the Hado by the hand by the end? And why does Street Fighter feel notably incomplete as a movie? Let’s dive into the spoiler zone!

To be fair, it is an intentional plot point that the tournament is all a ruse for Bison’s larger plan, which is something Ken himself doesn’t initially want to admit because it means so much to him. But still, it also feels weird how the tournament is handled in Street Fighter, because it does often feel like such an onscreen afterthought rather than a simple but effective way to give us more crowd-pleasing one-on-one fights in a movie called Street Fighter.

Ken at least gets two big tournament brawls, as he first faces Balrog (Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson) and then Dhalsim (Vidyut Jammwal), coming out as the victor in both cases, which sends him to the finals. But then there are the fights that are completely kept offscreen to a maddening extent, as Guile (Cody Rhodes) is defeated by Vega (Orville Peck), yet we don’t see a second of it, just the aftermath, as we’re told Vega won and see the large triple cuts on Guile’s face. And still, that’s somehow better than the Zangief (Olivier Richters) and Dhalsim showdown, which isn’t even verbally mentioned , but only available as info via quick flashes on the screen of the World Warrior board. Dhalsim at least gets a little more to do in the movie beyond this, but poor Zangief is bizarrely removed from sight for the entire tournament, never seen again after a group tussle everyone gets into at a club the night before the tournament begins. We never see him have an official fight, we never see his loss, and we never see him depart. He just ghosts the movie.

Come on, Street Fighter filmmakers, if you don’t want to give these other fights their own full scene, that’s where the power of a fight montage can come in handy!

Then there are the multiple outright forfeits that occur during the tournament, which again, is intentional thanks to Bison, even as you wonder how frustrating this would be for those tuning in to watch what appears to be a very big, internationally popular event. First, because Bison has Ryu held captive, he has Ryu officially listed as dropping out of the tournament, meaning his opponent, Joe (Alexander Volkanovski), wins by forfeit. Then Joe’s next opponent, Vega, also drops out of the tournament, presumably because he’s one of Bison’s main henchmen and his boss has work for him closer to home that can’t wait.

So Joe just forfeits all the way to the finals against Ken… Except then Ken never shows up for the final fight, because he goes to help rescue Ryu. Meaning Joe never has a single fight but is still the official winner of the World Warrior tournament! Which could have been a fun bit, but Joe is barely shown at all prior to his “win,” so it’s not like there’s even much resonance to this happening, beyond the humor for longtime Street Fighter fans of freaking non-playable original game character Joe to be elevated like this (albeit quite briefly).

Going back to the in-universe viewership of the tournament, it also stands out that Ken and Ryu are both well known fighters in the film, and it’s actually mentioned on TV what a big deal it is that they’ll both be in the tournament after years of separation, complete with the tantalizing promise of getting to see them battle one another. But while we moviegoers do get to see Ken and Ryu fight in an alley brawl at one point, working their old issues out the only way they know how, you gotta assume folks were pissed when Ryu was a no show at that heavily publicized tournament. I know Bison is a full-on dictator with bigger, more ominous goals, but still, there’s gonna be some super pissed-off comments and tweets about the whole “No Ryu” debacle.

Amusingly, outside of seeing the death of Ken and Ryu’s master, Gouken (Don Lee), in the film’s animated flashbacks, there’s only one named character who meets their end in Street Fighter – and it’s the one and only Joe.

Yes, poor Joe gets to experience some major highs and lows in a matter of minutes, as he’s declared the winner of the tournament by announcer Don Sauvage (Eric André), only for Akuma (Joe "Roman Reigns" Anoa'i) to appear out of nowhere and demand to face the winner. Unimpressed when he sees Joe, given he arrived assuming he’d be facing Ryu, Akuma is also quick to respond when Joe tries to challenge him, using his demonic powers to literally blow Joe up.

Street Fighter seems overly busy on the villain front as it heads towards its conclusion. There’s the obvious threat throughout the film of Bison, who’s got a cadre of formidable fighters working for him, including Vega, Cammy (Mel Jarnson), and Juli (Rayna Vallandingham). But then there’s the otherworldly power of Akuma, who Ryu is particularly fearful of, haunted by the fact that it was his own dabbling with an inner darkness that seemed to call to Akuma when Ryu won the last tournament, only for Akuma to kill Gouken. But that means Ryu is also fearful of himself , since he is worried that fighting again will lead to him succumbing to the dark urges Gouken warned him about, and which he tapped into when he violently defeated Sagat in the first tournament.

So how does Street Fighter juggle these three different potential big bads in the form of Akuma, Evil Ryu and Bison? Awkwardly, as you might expect when a movie is packing all of this into the very first film in a relaunched franchise. After Akuma kills Joe, Ryu arrives to confront him, and Akuma goes very Palpatine/Darth Vader by actively encouraging Ryu to use his dark side to unleash in their battle – which is exactly what Ryu eventually does. With Bison watching this confrontation from the arena’s otherwise empty stands, Ryu’s white gi magically turns black, as Evil Ryu battles Akuma and is eventually able to overpower him, knocking him out in the process.

That’s when Ken, Chun-Li and Dan Hibiki (Andrew Schulz, in a role way more prominent than Dan’s game history would ever have you expect) arrive, thinking it’s time to celebrate their friend’s victory, only for Evil Ryu to attack them too. He completely incapacitates both Dan and Chun-Li with one hit each, which is pretty insulting to Chun-Li; let her at least get in more offense than freaking Dan! But when Evil Ryu seems ready to outright kill them, he’s suddenly hit with a Hadouken! Yes, Ken has finally been able to unlock this most special of special moves too, something we’d seen him try and fail to do throughout the movie. And Ken’s Hadouken is so special that just the one apparently was enough to turn Evil Ryu good again right away, as Ryu oddly never really has to deal with quelling the darkness in himself – he just needed his best bro to blast him with blue energy! Hey, if it works, it works, right?

When it briefly seems Ryu might have actually taken a fatal hit from Ken, Ken sings “What’s Up?” – he and Ryu’s favorite song – to his old buddy, which finally leads Ryu to slowly come to and begin to sing along, soon joined by a tearful Chun-Li, Dan, and even Don Sauvage, who awakens from the rubble he was knocked into earlier by Akuma. And hey, kudos to 4 Non Blonds, because “What’s Up?” remains a great song 33 years after it came out, and between its prominent use in both Street Fighter and Masters of the Universe, they are killing it on licensing this year.

With the whole Evil Ryu deal dealt with easier than one might think, that means it’s finally time to take on Bison! …Except that doesn’t happen at all, because Bison and his goons sneak away, taking the knocked out Akuma with them.

Realizing what Bison now has gotten ahold of, and how it could give him the power he was trying to gain from Ryu, Dan asks “Did we make things worse?” Our heroes try to follow, but are stopped by Cammy pulling out a goddamn rocket launcher from Bison’s fleeing vehicle, which she uses to blow up Chun-Li’s van. So now our heroes have to figure out how to give chase a different way, in what feels like a bit of an odd move structure-wise for a movie that earlier felt like it was nearing its climax, but now clearly still has so much left in play!

…Except then the movie just ends. Okay, there’s one more scene, but it’s still bizarre how Street Fighter doesn’t actually offer a conclusion. There’s a line between having a fun sequel tease after you wrap up your film’s main storyline and simply not wrapping up and leaving any sense of closure, and Street Fighter definitely crosses that line.

The film’s final scene finds Ken, Ryu, Chun-Li and Dan on the side of the road, trying to hitchhike. And lo and behold, a car does pull over for them with Guile and Dhalsim inside, who we learned earlier were also both at the tournament on a mission to stop Bison… even though we then never saw them intervene at all after that. But now they’re for real tracking Bison, so they give the others a ride, with the six Street Fighters packing into the too-small car and turning up the radio to sing along to “It’s Raining Men” (sure, why not?) as they drive off into the distance and into the closing credits.

And again, I gotta stress, this all feels super weird, because it just seems like the movie stops rather than properly ends, completely putting off any sort of showdown with Bison – even one that could have ended with “We’ll meet again.”

Hell, we never even get any sort of fight between Chun-Li and Cammy, despite several scenes used to set them up as major rivals, priming the audience for an impending showdown. But as it turns out, that too is something that is tabled for the future. All of which is a rather vexing way to have things play out.

After the film’s main credits play at the end, with fun visuals for the cast that use the same art and graphics as the individual character posters for the film, we cut to a mid-credits scene.

This dialogue-free sequence returns to the animated segments that opened Street Fighter and were used throughout the film for flashbacks. The opening sequence showed Ryu defeating Sagat – a high-profile game character who was notably absent from the live-action portions of the film – in the first World Warrior tournament, but only after he tapped into his Evil Ryu powers, slicing Sagat’s chest open with a mystically-powered punch up his body.

The mid-credit scene shows Sagat again, years later, and now bearing the familiar large scar from the games up his torso, the result of Ryu’s actions. Sagat is seen using his martial arts prowess to knock down a palm tree, as one does, only for him to turn to find a floating Bison before him, with Vega, Juli and Cammy at his side.

Obviously, this is a set-up for Sagat to join Bison’s team in a potential Street Fighter sequel, while Sagat only being seen as a dialogue-free animated figure also means they still have the flexibility to cast whoever they wish as the character next time out, not having to match anything specifically established here on the live-action front. And presumably, Sagat would now be seeking revenge against Ryu…

...but also, can they remember they forgot to have Chun-Li and Cammy fight next time and remedy that, please?

articles.title: Super Smash Bros. Player Mew2King Banned From Tournament After Bug Bites Spark Health Concerns
articles.summary: Professional Super Smash Bros. player Jason ‘Mew2King’ Zimmerman has been banned from a competitive tournament after posting photos of his concerning skin condition and complaining of a bug infestation in his home.
articles.body:
Professional Super Smash Bros. player Jason ‘Mew2King’ Zimmerman has been banned from a competitive tournament after posting photos of his concerning skin condition and complaining of a bug infestation in his home.

On the morning of October 16, 2026, Zimmerman found himself going viral due to a thread of posts he’d published on Twitter/X the day before. In the posts, he complained of suffering from swelling hands, which he attributed to either playing too much without rest or being bitten by bugs in his home.

“My hands are slightly swollen (could be from all the SSBM Fox or from the bugs in the house that bite me each day), like pink/red and puffy/fatter than usual, is there a way to fix this ASAP? I'm boarding my flight to Texas now,” he wrote.

He went on to share a photo of his hand and one of his right leg, which was covered in red, painful-looking bumps that appeared to be bug bites. Zimmerman claimed that these bites happen to him “every week,” and are a driving factor in his decision to move from Ohio to California.

“I had like a hundred of these on my body two months ago. Like, my entire body. This isn’t even nearly the worst picture, not even close,” he explained in another post. “It’s all bug bites from the house. Lived like that for all year. Or recent months.”

Needless to say, fans were fairly concerned about Zimmerman’s health and living conditions, with many theorizing that he was dealing with a bed bug infestation. Others urged him against getting on a plane or staying in a hotel, saying that he might spread the supposed bed bugs, which are known for sneaking into luggage and clothing to lay eggs at their next destination.

News of Zimmerman’s condition quickly spread online, prompting no end of discourse within the fighting game community — to the point where the tournament he was competing in, Xtreme Fighters Showdown, outright banned him from the event.

The tournament’s CEO published a statement about the situation on Twitter/X, alerting the public that Mew2King was no longer invited to take part in the competition as a direct result of his health issues.

“For the safety of our event, XFS 2026, we have politely informed Mew2King he will not be able to participate or attend our event this weekend due to a self-reported health concern,” the statement reads. “The health and wellbeing of our attendees is our priority. Thank you, and we’ll see you this weekend.”

The health and wellbeing of our attendees is our priority. Thank you, and we’ll see you this weekend. — Xtreme Fighters Showdown (@xfshowdown) October 16, 2026

The health and wellbeing of our attendees is our priority. Thank you, and we’ll see you this weekend.

Zimmerman has not provided any public updates after this latest development, and has since deleted all the tweets discussing his skin condition.

And in September, Pokémon VGC regional champion Donghun Youm claimed that he lost a match due to his opponent's overwhelming stench , prompting a community-wide push for players to use deodorant at tournaments.

articles.title: James Gunn Shoots Down Milly Alcock Supergirl Rumors, Shares Man of Tomorrow Update
articles.summary: James Gunn has shot down rumors that Milly Alcock was fired as Supergirl and confirmed that he'll show Peter Safran an early cut of Man of Tomorrow later today.
articles.body:
James Gunn has shot down rumors that Milly Alcock was fired as Supergirl and confirmed that he'll show Peter Safran an early cut of Man of Tomorrow later today.

The DC Studios co-chairman took to Threads on October 16 to dispel rumors surrounding his comic book movie projects. Although he's found putting a lid on the endless flow of internet rumors to be a little tiring, there were a few he wanted to take aim at when replying to a fan on Twitter/X.

First and foremost was the rumor that director Matt Reeves had completely departed The Batman Part 2 as director. Just about everyone now confirmed to be involved in the Elseworlds sequel had already clarified that Reeves would remain involved, so his denial is no surprise here. Another more recent rumor had some fans saying the star of Supergirl was let go, but that one's not true, either.

Milly Alcock has deleted all the posts related to Supergirl including her announcement one 🙃 — Everything_DCU (@EverythingDCU_) October 15, 2026

Milly Alcock has deleted all the posts related to Supergirl including her announcement one 🙃

DC movie watchers feared the worst for Alcock's character after noticing the star had wiped mentions of Kara Zor-El from her Instagram timeline. Although that's not completely true – some photos and Reels related to Supergirl are still very much publicly visible – her standalone film's trouble in theaters had some believing she would be leaving the DCU behind.

Gunn confirmed that's not the case, and it's easy to see why. Alcock first appeared as the character in 2025's Superman and reprised her role in Supergirl when it came out in June. She's been firmly established in the new comic book movie universe, but she's also poised for a triumphant return in Man of Tomorrow .

Earlier this summer, Gunn teased that Alcock was set to return as Kara when the Superman sequel premieres July 2027. He even went as far as to say that her dynamic with David Corenswet's Clark Kent would come into play in the new movie while filming was underway recently.

James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow: Superman vs. Lex Luthor Art Gallery

Speaking of Man of Tomorrow, the third rumor Gunn shot down had to do with whispers that the DCU film had received poor reviews after an early test screening allegedly featured a dark ending and the death of a beloved hero. It's another bit of gossip that the director and comic book movie executive confirmed "couldn't be more false," but it also came with an update.

It just so happens that Gunn had planned to show Safran a director's cut for Man of Tomorrow later today. He said his fellow DC Studios co-chairman will "obviously" be the first person to see any version of the film, adding, "and that's a month early!"

Gunn's words come at a time that has DC fans more anxious than ever. Superman started the live-action corner of the DCU off with a sonic boom when it swooped into theaters last year, but that momentum came to a halt with Supergirl. Although Lanterns helped reignite the fan base with strong casting choices and a grounded story , there's been some hesitancy amongst those online who fear films like Clayface and Man of Tomorrow won't deliver.

Gunn, at least, sounds more confident than ever. As far as rumors go, while fans await official updates, there's only so much he's willing to entertain.

"Oh brother," his post said. "You guys just have to stop listening to BS, and I'm mostly done shooting down rumors, as there are so many and I'm not on here much."

If you weren't aware, the former Marvel filmmaker has put rumors on blast before. When fans started to suspect Supernatural star Jenson Ackles would be playing the DCU's Batman, for example, Gunn quickly stepped in to put an end to things .

For more while we wait to see how the DCU is coming together behind the scenes, you can read IGN's interview with Safran , where we learned about a few casting updates for the new Mr. Miracle series. You can also read about what's next for John Cena's Peacemaker .

articles.title: Red Rising Greenlit for Movie Adaptation With Author Pierce Brown to Produce
articles.summary: The Red Rising book series by author Pierce Brown has officially been greenlit for a movie adaptation from Paramount Pictures, with Hunger Games alum Francis Lawrence to direct.
articles.body:
The Red Rising book series by author Pierce Brown has officially been greenlit for a movie adaptation from Paramount Pictures, with Hunger Games alum Francis Lawrence to direct.

Red Rising is getting the Hollywood treatment more than a decade after it was first published in 2014. As confirmed by The Hollywood Reporter on October 16, Paramount Pictures has picked up the rights to the series, which will be brought to the screen by director Francis Lawrence.

Lawrence is known for his work on another young adult screen adaptation in the Hunger Games series, having directed every movie in the franchise sans the first one, which was directed by Gary Ross. Lawrence recently directed Stephen King adaptation The Long Walk , as well as the forthcoming Sunrise on the Reaping , the latest movie in the Hunger Games franchise.

Lawrence is also set to produce the Red Rising film alongside Cameron MacConomy for their about:blank production company, as well as Francesco Goedhuis and the author of the Red Rising saga himself, Pierce Brown.

Brown reacted to the news in a post on his Instagram account , writing, "Let fall the iron rain. Bloodydamn, I love this team."

Joining Red Rising is Justin Rhodes, who will write the movie’s script. Eagle-eyed IGN readers will recognize this name, as he is also involved in Netflix’s live-action Bioshock movie , which is reportedly still in early development. Rhodes is known for films like Terminator: Dark Fate, Traveler, and Liminal.

Red Rising is a sprawling book series that is planned to end with its seventh and final installment, which as yet has no release date. Set in a galaxy with a strict, color-coded caste system, the books follow Darrow, a Red — the lowest rank on the social totem pole. He and his fellow Reds toil tirelessly in the mines of Mars, with the hope that one day, they will be able to make the planet habitable for human life… but it turns out that this was already accomplished generations ago.

After learning of this massive betrayal, Darrow makes it his mission to infiltrate the highest social caste, the Golds, and set things right across the entire galaxy in a deadly conflict that spans more than a decade. If you're interested in getting into the books, you can check out our guide to navigating this sprawling adventure , which will no doubt come in handy once the movie eventually gets released.

articles.title: Valkyries fever sweeps Bay Area ahead of WNBA Finals opener
articles.summary: The countdown is on to Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, and after one final practice, the Valkyries say they're eager to take the court Saturday at Ballhalla again...
articles.body:
The Bay Area is buzzing as the Golden State Valkyries prepare for the biggest game in franchise history.

The countdown is on to Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, and after one final practice, the Valkyries say they're eager to take the court Saturday at Ballhalla against the Atlanta Dream.

With the anticipation building by the hour, head coach Natalie Nakase says her team is more than ready for the moment.

"We feel like caged animals, ready to get there into Ballhalla and play our best four quarters of defense," Nakase said.

The Valkyries have stormed into the Finals just two years after joining the league, a remarkable accomplishment that has captured the attention of basketball fans across the country.

Guard Veronica Burton says the excitement is impossible to ignore.

"The anticipation is building, but we're ready to play," Burton said.

Nakase credits the team's chemistry and selfless mindset for its rapid rise.

"Our players have big hearts. They always want success for their teammates more than for themselves. I think that's rare," she said.

Forward Gabby Williams believes staying composed under the bright lights of the championship stage will be key.

"Whoever stays the most composed will win," Williams said.

The Valkyries are expected to get a major boost from their home crowd.

Ballhalla has become one of the toughest venues in the league, with fans creating an electric atmosphere every game.

"We want to use Ballhalla to our advantage and get a good start," Williams said.

Meanwhile, the Atlanta Dream know exactly what they're walking into.

"It's going to be loud in there. There's a lot of excitement, probably some nerves, but I'm excited to be there," Dream guard Naz Hillmon said.

With the WNBA championship on the line and the Bay Area basketball spotlight shining bright, all eyes now turn to Ballhalla, where the Valkyries will look to take the first step toward a title on Saturday night.

Fans across the city are embracing the moment, from bars filled with supporters to elaborate neighborhood displays dedicated to the team.

One of the most visible tributes is "Boohalla," a Halloween-themed Valkyries display in the Inner Richmond District near Third Avenue and Clement Street.

Visitor Laura Louie said she was impressed by the attention to detail.

"It's amazing," Louie said. "They have everything. They have the flag. They have the whole roster with their Halloween dedicated names."

The display was created by San Francisco residents Ainsley Rossitto and Sarah Swig, both season ticket holders and longtime supporters of the Valkyries.

"We just love the fan base and the culture of the valkyries," Swig said. "To get to see people walking down the street and get to chit chat with people who are also Val fans has been really fun."

Rossitto highlighted one of her favorite parts of the installation.

"My favorite is, Natalie. I think we've recreated here as Natalie nacauldron," Rossitto said. "For boohalla and she's really cooking up some strategic plays."

The display also includes references to the Valkyries' playoff run.

"The sweeping with the aces card is really fun," Swig said.

Across town at Mother Bar in the Mission District, fans expressed excitement about the growing visibility of women's sports and the Valkyries' success.

"I'm so glad we're finally in an era where women's sports are getting the recognition they deserve. We're so excited," one fan said.

Another supporter cheered, "Ballhalla yeah. Valkyries yeah..."

Season ticket holder Miki Nakamura said she has been waiting years for a WNBA team in San Francisco.

"I've been waiting for a wnba team to be here in San Francisco. I'm beyond excited," Nakamura said.

As the Valkyries prepare for their first Finals game, supporters say the team's success has created a strong sense of community throughout the Bay Area.

Rossitto and Swig said they plan to be at Chase Center for Game 1.

"We'll be at the real Ballhalla," they said.

The Valkyries will host the Atlanta Dream on Saturday afternoon at Chase Center. Fans expect the sold-out crowd at "Ballhalla" to provide a significant home-court advantage as the franchise pursues its first WNBA championship.
